ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rhombus bridge circuit; the left and right two rhombus vertices are connected to the two ends of an external AC power supply V0; the upper and lower two rhombus vertices each lead out one open-circuit terminal, with the middle labeled output. The upper-left branch of the rhombus is an inductor L, the upper-right branch is a resistor R2, the lower-left branch is a resistor R1, and the lower-right branch is a capacitor C. Reasoning: Because the output terminal is open-circuit, the upper branch L-R2 and the lower branch R1-C can be regarded as two independent voltage dividers driven by the same input peak voltage V0. Take the left-to-right input phasor as V0. The upper output node phasor is Vtop/V0 = iωL/(R2+iωL). The lower output node phasor is Vbot/V0 = R1/(R1+1/(iωC)) = iωR1C/(1+iωR1C). Therefore the output transfer-function magnitude comes from H(ω)=Vout/V0 = iωL/(R2+iωL) - iωR1C/(1+iωR1C), and the output polarity only affects the sign and does not affect the magnitude. Let a=ωL/R2, b=ωR1C, then b=ka, where k=R1 R2 C/L = 3×2×4/5 = 24/5 = 4.8. Thus H=ia/(1+ia)-ib/(1+ib), so |H|=|b-a|/sqrt((1+a^2)(1+b^2)) = (k-1)a/sqrt((1+a^2)(1+k^2a^2)). Maximizing this expression is equivalent to maximizing its square, obtaining that the maximum value occurs at a^2=1/k. At this time |H|max=(k-1)/(k+1)=3.8/5.8≈0.655. The input peak value V0=1 V, so the maximum instantaneous output voltage magnitude is approximately 0.655 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit from the image: label the left and right diamond vertices as the input terminals of the AC source, the top and bottom vertices as the open output terminals, with L on the upper-left side, R2 on the upper-right side, R1 on the lower-left side, and C on the lower-right side. Since the output is open, treat the upper and lower paths as two independent voltage dividers driven by the same phasor input V0. From the text use L=5 H, C=4 F, R1=3 ohm, R2=2 ohm, and peak input V0=1 V. Let the left-to-right source phasor be V0. The top output-node phasor is Vtop/V0 = iωL/(R2+iωL), and the bottom output-node phasor is Vbot/V0 = R1/(R1+1/(iωC)). Therefore H(ω)=Vout/V0 = iωL/(R2+iωL) - iωR1C/(1+iωR1C), up to an irrelevant sign depending on output polarity. Define a=ωL/R2 and b=ωR1C, so b=ka with k=R1 R2 C/L = 24/5 = 4.8. Then H = ia/(1+ia) - ib/(1+ib), giving |H| = |b-a|/sqrt((1+a^2)(1+b^2)) = (k-1)a/sqrt((1+a^2)(1+k^2a^2)). Maximize this with respect to a, e.g. by differentiating the squared magnitude; the maximum occurs at a^2=1/k. The maximum value is (k-1)/(k+1)=3.8/5.8=0.655..., and multiplying by V0=1 V gives about 0.65 V.

method.method_draft: First read the image as an AC bridge: the input source is applied between the left and right vertices, and the output is the open-circuit voltage between the top and bottom bridge nodes. Assign the four bridge arms as ZL=iωL on the upper-left side, R2 on the upper-right side, R1 on the lower-left side, and ZC=1/(iωC) on the lower-right side. From the text insert L=5 H, C=4 F, R1=3 ohm, R2=2 ohm, V0=1 V. Use the Wheatstone-bridge midpoint formula: Vout/V0 = ZL/(ZL+R2) - R1/(R1+ZC) = (ZL ZC - R1 R2)/((ZL+R2)(R1+ZC)). Since ZL ZC = L/C, the numerator is frequency independent: |L/C - R1R2|. Thus maximizing output over the unknown frequency is equivalent to minimizing |ZL+R2||R1+ZC|. Its squared magnitude is (R2^2+ω^2L^2)(R1^2+1/(ω^2C^2)). Minimize this expression using AM-GM or differentiation; the minimum denominator magnitude is R1R2 + L/C. Therefore |Vout|max = V0 |R1R2 - L/C|/(R1R2 + L/C) = |6 - 1.25|/(6 + 1.25) = 4.75/7.25 = 0.655..., so the requested magnitude is about 0.65 V.

Let a=ωL/R2, b=ωR1C, then b=ka, where k=R1 R2 C/L = 3×2×4/5 = 24/5 = 4.8. Thus H=ia/(1+ia)-ib/(1+ib), so |H|=|b-a|/sqrt((1+a^2)(1+b^2)) = (k-1)a/sqrt((1+a^2)(1+k^2a^2)). Maximizing this expression is equivalent to maximizing its square, obtaining that the maximum value occurs at a^2=1/k. At this time |H|max=(k-1)/(k+1)=3.8/5.8≈0.655. The input peak value V0=1 V, so the maximum instantaneous output voltage magnitude is approximately 0.655 V.
